thread:
Maya (SRE): :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: spike of 429s from Okta JWKS endpoint, multiple token verifications failing across prod services (console + API). Getting a lot of `jwt: signature verification failed` logs. Impacting: web console login, background API auth for ingestion pipeline. Root alert at 1962156789.

PagerDuty: Incident triggered by 3 services failing auth check in >5m window.

Maya (SRE): Quick status — can folks confirm scope? Are we seeing start-of-failure ~ 04:14 UTC?

Raj (Auth): Confirmed. Logs show repeated 429s when our token-validator fetches JWKS from `https://company.okta.com/.well-known/jwks.json`. Rate-limited by Okta. Sample log lines:```
2026-11-03T04:14:28Z auth-validator ERROR fetch_jwks failed status=429 url=https://company.okta.com/.well-known/jwks.json
2026-11-03T04:14:30Z api-gateway WARN token verify failed err="jwks fetch rate limited"
```

Sylvie (oncall): I'm oncall — collecting impact. CS - Hana, any customer tickets yet?

CS - Hana: We're getting 5 inbound tickets about console login failures from enterprise customers. No major outages reported externally yet but customers are blocked from console access.

Leo (Platform): Our services use short JWKS TTL (60s) which explains the flood. Okta appears to be enforcing a low requests-per-minute for the JWKS endpoint.

Maya (SRE): Mitigation idea set 1: extend local JWKS cache TTL and stop aggressive refetching. Can push a hotfix to token-validator lib to bump TTL to 15m and use stale-while-revalidate on 429s.

Raj (Auth): Agree. I can cut a small patch to our shared auth lib. Patch will: 1) increase local cache ttl to 900s, 2) on 429 return cached keys (if available) and log a rate-limit metric, 3) backoff jitter for refetch. Patch ready to test.

Leo (Platform): How invasive is the rollout? We have the library pinned in 4 services (api-gateway, console, ingestion, admin-api). We can rollout canary to console first then API gateway.

Maya (SRE): Priority: console logins are highest impact. Raj, can you produce a patched package and a canary image to deploy to console within 15-20 minutes? I'll coordinate traffic routing.

Raj (Auth): Yes. Building now. CI should finish in ~8m.

Incident Bot: Incident created: INC-20261103-OKTA-JWKS-429. Severity: SEV2. PagerDuty notified: oncall.

PagerDuty: Paging Sylvie (oncall) — acknowledged.

Sylvie (oncall): Acknowledged. Handoff: I'm taking ownership until resolved. Quick summary for next shift: Root cause likely Okta rate-limiting JWKS. Impact: console + API auth failures; customer console access degraded. Current mitigation in progress: patch to auth lib to use cached JWKS on 429s and extend TTL.

Maya (SRE): Temporary workaround until rollout: increase `JWKS_CACHE_TTL` env var in console deployment to 900 (was 60). If we can't deploy patched lib fast enough we can patch deployment env.

Leo (Platform): I'm pushing a config change to console staging first to validate, then prod. Command:```
kubectl set env deployment/console JWKS_CACHE_TTL=900 -n prod
```
Applying now.

Leo (Platform): Applied to console prod. Observability: increasing cache TTL should reduce outgoing JWKS requests. Watching metrics: `outgoing.okta.jwks_requests` and `auth.token_verify_failures`.

Maya (SRE): After TTL change we should see an immediate drop in JWKS requests. If token verifications are still failing, patch rollout is next.

(~3m later) Raj (Auth): Build succeeded: `auth-lib@2.4.1-jwks-backoff`. I published the package and created docker image `auth-sidecar:2.4.1-jwks-backoff`.

Raj (Auth): Plan: 1) deploy to console canary (1 pod), 2) run smoke auth tests for 10m, 3) if green, sequentially roll to api-gateway and ingestion.

Maya (SRE): Can we also add a short-circuit that when Okta returns 429 we treat as transient and let cached token verification succeed? That's in the patch, right?

Raj (Auth): Yes. Implementation: on 429 -> if cache exists return cached keys and mark `okta.rate_limit=true` metric. Only if no cache fallback exists do we fail token validation.

Support Ops: Noted several customers are asking for ETA. Recommend templated customer message: "We're investigating a third-party authentication provider issue affecting console login. Mitigation in progress; next update in 30 minutes." Hana, can you draft?

CS - Hana: Drafted and sent to Slack #customer-updates. Will post after 15m if impact persists.

Maya (SRE): Rolling out canary now to console. Leo please add a tag to the pod: `canary-authlib=2.4.1` and route 2% traffic.

Leo (Platform): Canary up (pod console-7c9d-canary). Routing 2% traffic via Istio virtualservice. Smoke tests running (login flow).

(Observability) Maya (SRE): auth.token_verify_failures down from ~120/min to ~8/min after cache TTL and canary patch showing fewer errors. outgoing.okta.jwks_requests down 85%.

Sylvie (oncall): Good. Keep canary for 20m then ramp. I'll coordinate with Raj for roll to gateways. I'm updating the incident doc with current mitigations and timeline.

Raj (Auth): After 20m canary looks stable. Starting rolling update to api-gateway (gradual, 5% steps).

Maya (SRE): Noting one peculiar thing: ingestion service still showing occasional `signature verification failed` for long-lived tokens issued after 03:50 UTC. Raj, could be token rotation issue or a clock skew. Can you check?

Raj (Auth): Investigating ingestion logs. Also verified system clocks via NTP; skew <2s. Found that ingestion sometimes drops cache on OOM and then tries to re-fetch during high load -> hits 429. We'll patch service to be more resilient to cache eviction (preload keys at startup and on OOM).

Leo (Platform): Increasing memory for ingestion pods to reduce OOMs as a stopgap. `kubectl patch deployment/ingestion -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"ingestion","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"1Gi"}}}]}}}}'` Applying.

Support Ops: Customers on support queue are being updated (Hana). No escalations to legal/exec yet.

(1h later) Maya (SRE): Rollout complete across console, api-gateway, ingestion, admin-api. Metrics stable, token verification failures returned to baseline. Okta confirmed they throttled JWKS endpoint due to unusual traffic pattern from our region; working with Okta on long-term rate limit increase.

Sylvie (oncall): Incident summary for handoff: cause = Okta JWKS rate-limit (429s) causing token verification failures; mitigations = increased local JWKS cache TTL, patched auth-lib to return cached keys on 429 and backoff, increased ingestion memory to reduce OOMs, staged rollouts; customer comms sent. Status = degraded -> recovering -> resolved-with-followup.

Maya (SRE): Filing follow-ups: 1) Request rate-limit exception with Okta + ensure our JWKS request pattern is spread (introduce jitter). 2) Make cache TTL configurable per service (default 15m). 3) Add fallback metrics/alert for sustained JWKS 429 rate. 4) Postmortem draft assigned to Raj.

Raj (Auth): Taking postmortem. ETA for draft: EOD today.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-20261103-OKTA-JWKS-429 -> marked RESOLVED.

Sylvie (oncall): Closing handoff to next oncall at 1962157420. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
